rationale: Both use memoized recursion over sorted count tuples. A tries every subset of titles through a bitmask. That is exhaustive, so it is obviously correct, and the loop is easy to follow even though the valid flag is a bit clunky. B prunes the search to 'take one copy from each of the g most plentiful titles'. That rule is valid, but its correctness rests on an argument the reader has to accept. B also writes the recursion as a deeply nested min/tuple/sorted/generator expression that is hard to read and debug. B has nicer module documentation and is more efficient, but it hardcodes titles 1-5 when counting, whereas A's Counter-based counting does not depend on title values. A's straightforward and transparently correct search wins on clarity.
